gallery.description: Painting of the nun Hillegond Gerritsdr, who became a nun in the St Anna cloister of Haarlem ca 1530. She was probably Marten van Heemskerck's sister-in-law. She was a wealthy Catholic and is portrayed with a rosary. When she died she left all of her possessions, including this painting, to the Hofje van Codde and Beresteyn, where it hung for centuries in the regent's room. Now on loan to the Frans Hals Museum in Haarlem.

gallery.title: File:Playing bears van beresteyn.JPG
gallery.credit: Own work foto of sculpture by Frank Letterie, information: here
gallery.description: Statue of two playing bears in the Ripperdastraat. This statue is a memorial to the Hofje van Codde en van Berensteijn. The statue and the hofje were both formerly located at the train station square in Haarlem, the Netherlands. Temporarily placed in the Ripperdastraat, this statue was ordered in 1969 when the Haarlem Railway Station annexed the land formerly owned by the Hofje that then relocated to the Jos Cuyperstraat. The statue was placed on Stationsplein in 1978. The bears were a reference to the "bears" in the coat of arms of the family Berensteijn that founded the Berensteijn half of the hofje foundation still bearing that name. The Codde hofje was added in 1731. The bears of the family Berensteijn (also spelled Berensteyn) heraldic shield were originally wild swine "beren", not brown bears, as this sculpture suggests.

gallery.description: Painting of Beresteyn-van der Eem family, originally in the possession of the Hofje Codde en van Beresteyn. Sold in 1885 (after hanging for 200 years in the Hofje) to the Louvre as a Frans Hals painting. Painting is typical of other period family portraits from Holland, with an attachment on the right for a child born later, but also showing the children from the first marriage of Paulus van Beresteyn as well as Nicolaes and Emerentia, the children of Catharina van der Eem. The painting has been restored and painted over several times. It is probably by Pieter Claesz Soutman, who was a regent of the Hofje, and not Frans Hals.

gallery.filename: Hofje Codde en van Beresteyn memorial.jpg
gallery.title: File:Hofje Codde en van Beresteyn memorial.jpg
gallery.description: Memorial that used to be in the Hofje van Beresteijn in Haarlem on the Lange Molenstraat, across the Haarlem railway station. Expansion of the station led to the demolishing of the building in 1969. This memorial was relocated when the Hofje moved and now hangs on the wall of the regent's room in the newly built Hofje on the J. Cuypersstraat, Haarlem. Photo of the current situation.
